carried_forward.title: an unknown delivery does not fence later same-conversation parts
carried_forward.verified_against_current_source: unchanged; every citation in the prior report re-checked at 582ae55, no source movement
carried_forward.recommendation: at the existing CommsOutbox eligibility/claim seam, make a pending delivery ineligible while an earlier same-conversation delivery is claimed or unknown past its send boundary; keep independent conversations drainable and the bounded batch

carried_forward.title: comms_gateway_test test-shape items (DEAD/TEST/DUP)
carried_forward.judgment: DEAD and DUP recorded fixed in that document; TEST remains deferred there and its source-side equivalent does not exist in tamoz-comms-gateway/lib - the raw-SQL probes work around a missing public observable-outbox read seam owned by CommsStore (F07/F11), not by this gem
carried_forward.recommendation: none for F12; tracked with the CommsStore projection work

findings.title: the delivery outbox has no attempt bound and no terminal exhausted state
findings.recommendation: have claim_delivery refuse a re-claim once the row's already-bound effect-journal attempt count reaches the descriptor's retry ceiling, surfacing the existing :not_claimable path; no new machinery

findings.title: retry backoff and throttle deadlines are process-local
findings.recommendation: none required for correctness - the delivered-message deadline is durable (reserve_delivery_slot/defer_delivery) so a restart causes no send burst; if wanted, persist the failure streak through the @store the loop already holds

findings.title: the plaintext pairing-code memo is process-local and dies with the gateway
findings.recommendation: none at the gateway seam - never persisting the plaintext is the safe direction and pruning is correctly bounded by the live durable pending set; if the restart cost matters, re-issue on first post-restart contact via the existing issue_pairing_code path

findings.title: an exhausted or persistently failing delivery never becomes visible as a terminal state
findings.recommendation: resolve together with F12-COR-01 - once an attempt count exists, extend the existing DELIVERY_WORDS projection with the stuck fact; no separate metric or log subsystem

findings.title: the gem owns no process lifecycle; signals and supervision live in the CLI
findings.recommendation: one line in the gem README naming the caller as the signal/supervision owner; documentation only, no code change

verified_non_findings.claim: the gateway holds the bot token and never constructs a session or opens a workspace file
verified_non_findings.evidence: no File./Dir./IO./Pathname/open( anywhere in the gem; only require set is tamoz/comms, time, json and 11 require_relative siblings; the sole 'session' match in lib is a user-facing reply string; @controls is caller-injected and the production wiring returns nil

verified_non_findings.claim: the drainer never blindly retries an unknown row
verified_non_findings.evidence: drain_once selects only pending rows; an ambiguous send is marked unknown; only the operator's resolve_delivery (status = 'unknown' guard) can leave that state

verified_non_findings.claim: two gateway processes cannot drain the same outbox row
verified_non_findings.evidence: claim_delivery is a row-local compare-and-set and mark_delivery/send-started match owner AND fence; /tmp/probe_ttl.rb proved a TTL-expired stale owner gets :not_claimable at the send boundary and sends nothing
verified_non_findings.residual: the ordering side of concurrency (a second owner draining a successor row) is the carried-forward comms-unknown-ordering finding

verified_non_findings.claim: control commands are gated by the same allowlist as task text
verified_non_findings.evidence: Admission.decide resolves binding and surface before branching to command_admission; an unauthorized sender is ignore(:unbound) and never reaches command_disposition; control request ids are keyed on update_id so replay is bounded
